summary: Defines a Link-attributes sub-TLV carried inside TLV 22 to flood certain link characteristics in IS-IS. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A little note attached to a road in the map that says something special about it.

questions: what is the is-is link attribute sub-tlv
what does the local protection available bit mean
subtitle: A small optional flag field in IS-IS that tells other routers whether a link has local protection.

tldr.problem: IS-IS routers flood information about their links, but there was no standard place to advertise whether a link is protected by a local repair mechanism or should be avoided when computing repair paths.
tldr.mechanism: A new Link-attributes sub-TLV, sub-type 19, is carried inside TLV 22 and holds a 16-bit flags field with two defined bits.
tldr.outcome: Routers that do not understand the sub-TLV silently ignore it, so it can be deployed incrementally. The RFC is a Proposed Standard that has since been updated by RFC 9650.

facts.label: Link excluded from local protection path

today: RFC 5029 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 9650. It has not been obsoleted according to the unit's metadata.

sections.title: Background: IS-IS, TLVs and Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
IS-IS is the routing protocol specified in ISO 10589, with IPv4 support added in RFC 1195. A router advertises one or several Link State Protocol data units, which are built from variable-length tuples called TLVs (Type-Length-Value).

RFC 3784 defined new TLVs to add information about link characteristics, widen the range of IS-IS metrics and optimize the encoding of prefixes. This document adds one new sub-TLV, named Link-attributes, to the extended IS reachability TLV (type 22) from that RFC.
sections.eli5: A router tells its neighbors about its roads using little labelled boxes of information. This RFC adds a new kind of box that can go inside one of the existing boxes.

sections.title: The Link-Attributes Sub-TLV Format
sections.content:
The sub-TLV is carried within TLV 22 and uses the same format as the sub-TLVs of the traffic engineering extensions in RFC 3784: 1 octet of sub-type, 1 octet giving the length of the value, then the value. Here the value is a 16-bit flags field. The sub-type is 19 and the length is 2 octets.

The sub-TLV is OPTIONAL and MUST appear at most once for a single IS neighbor. If a received Link State Packet (LSP) contains more than one, an implementation SHOULD consider only the first one it finds.
sections.eli5: The sticker has a label saying what kind it is, a note of how big it is, and two on/off switches inside.

sections.title: The Defined Flag Bits
sections.content:
Two bits are defined in the flags field.

  • Local Protection Available (0x01): when set, the link is protected by some local protection mechanism, for example the fast reroute extensions of RFC 4090.
  • Link excluded from local protection path (0x02): when set, this link SHOULD not be included in any computation of a repair path by any other router in the routing area.

What causes a router to set the second bit is out of the scope of this document.
sections.eli5: One switch says 'this road has a backup road ready'. The other says 'please do not send detour traffic down this road'.

sections.title: Routers That Do Not Support It
sections.content: A router that does not support the link-attribute sub-TLV just silently ignores it. Since the sub-TLV is also optional, routers that do and do not understand it can sit in the same network without changing how they otherwise behave.
sections.eli5: If a router does not know what the sticker means, it just does not look at it, and everything else keeps working.

sections.title: IANA Code Points
sections.content:
IANA assigned codepoint 19 for the link-attribute sub-TLV carried within TLV 22. IANA also created a registry for the bit values inside the sub-TLV, with initial contents 0x1 (Local Protection Available) and 0x2 (Link Excluded from Local Protection).

Further values are to be allocated by the Standards Action process defined in RFC 2434, with Early Allocation (defined in RFC 4020) permitted.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of what each switch means, and adding a new switch needs a proper standards process.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This document raises no new issues beyond the opportunity for LSPs to be snooped and modified, which it does not make easier or harder. Because LSPs may now carry additional information about router capabilities, that information also becomes available to an attacker.

Specifications based on this mechanism need to describe the security considerations around disclosure and modification of their information. An integrity mechanism such as the one in RFC 3567 should be applied if modifying capability information carries a high risk.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can peek at the router's messages could read the stickers too, so if that matters, the messages should be sealed.

fields.name: Flags
fields.desc: Bit flags: 0x01 Local Protection Available, 0x02 Link excluded from local protection path.
